description:
FILED s429 (Fable), found by the #259 matrix (16 prototype shapes x 10 call contexts vs
perl; docs/session-log.md s429).  PRE-EXISTING (same rows on 374fcf7 and after #259).

  sub f ($) { "f(" . join(",", @_) . ")" }   print "R=", f "a" . "b", "\n";
      perl: R=f(ab)      PCL: R=f(a)b        <- named unary binds LOOSER than `.`
  same for (;$), (*), (_).  And for (*) only:
  sub g (*) { ... }   print "R=", g + 1, "\n";
      perl: R=g(1)       PCL: R=g(1,\n)      <- _proto_max_args declines `*`, so no comma narrowing

WHY: Pl/PExpr.pm handle_subcalls has TWO operand sites.  The named-unary site
(`is_named_unary($name)`, Config's table of BUILTIN named unaries: defined/ref/length/...)
runs the walker, the legacy branches, THEN `_extend_high_prec` (`length $s . "x"` ->
length($s . "x")).  The strictly-single site (`$no_pars` == 1 or [..1], user `($)`-class
subs and Config-1 builtins like shift/close/fileno) runs the walker + bareword-filehandle
branch and NO `_extend_high_prec`.  After #259 a user `($)`/`(;$)`/`(*)`/`(_)`/`(\@)`
sub's parse spec is 1 / [0,1] â perl's "named unary operator" exactly â so the
perl-faithful shape is: a user unary-class sub takes the NAMED-UNARY site (the
`is_named_unary` predicate answers yes for a declared sub whose _proto_parse_spec is
1 or [0,1]), and the strictly-single site is left to Config's non-named-unary
1-arg builtins.  That fixes both rows at once (the Operator branch there goes through
_extend_high_prec, which stops at the comma).  Probe the breaking case: `f FH, 1` for a
user `(*)` sub (bareword filehandle arg; the strictly-single site's bareword branch vs
the named-unary site's `_extend_high_prec` on a Word), and `close F, ...` (Config, must
stay).  Bar: the 4-population A/B (tools/emission-ab.pl) + gate; the matrix files in
the s429 scratch recipe are the acceptance rows (re-generate from the session-log table).
Sibling copies to check (rule 11): PExpr.pm:5893 `$prev_is_named_unary` also consults
is_named_unary.


=== s438b (Opus 5, 2026-08-23) DONE, exactly the shape this task ruled: the two
operand sites become ONE for the shape they share.  `Pl::PExpr::is_named_unary`
now answers for a DECLARED sub whose prototype's parse class is perl's
named-unary one -- `_proto_parse_spec` returning 1 (`($)`, `(*)`, `(_)`,
`(\@)`) or [0,1] (the `;`-led `(;$)`) -- via a new `_declared_named_unary`
helper.  The environment record is the ONLY second source: `known_no_of_params`
is deliberately NOT consulted, because its 1 covers Config builtins (shift,
close, fileno, eof) that are not named unaries and must stay at the
strictly-single site, whose bareword-filehandle branch is why it exists.
Config's table is asked FIRST, so a builtin's name keeps meaning the builtin.

That one predicate fixes both halves the task reported, because the
named-unary site runs `_extend_high_prec` and the strictly-single site does
not, and because `is_named_unary` is the strictly-single site's own guard:

  sub f ($) {...}  print f "a" . "b"   f(a)b   -> f(ab)     = perl
  sub f ($) {...}  print f $x + 1      1       -> f(6)      = perl
  sub g (*) {...}  print "R=", g + 1   g(1,\n) -> g(1)      = perl

MEASURED, and the answer is why the guard file exists: emission is IDENTICAL
across every population -- corpus-diff 111 files identical (silent drops 5
unchanged), and tools/emission-ab.pl over lib/**.pm + cpan-tests/** + perl's
own t/ = 951 files, SAME 951, DIFF 0, RCDIFF 0.  So no corpus can guard this
and the s371 rule applies: probes + guard rows ARE the bar.  RCDIFF 0 over 951
files is also the die-scan (the named-unary site's #153-step-5 `die` never
fires).  Per the WHAT-TO-RUN table (Pl/** + corpus-diff identical + lib
byte-identical + not a name-resolution change) no sweep was run.

Guard `Pl/t/user-unary-01.t`, 12 both_agree rows against live perl, 19 s: 7
positives (the four unary-class prototypes through `.`/`+`/`*`, the comma
boundary, a negative literal) and 5 negatives that are as load-bearing (`($;$)`
and `(@)` stay list operators, a TRAILING `;` in `($;)` keeps it one,
`close F` keeps the strictly-single site, `length` unchanged).  Inverse guard
run: on a fe46c7b worktree rows 1-7 FAIL and 8-12 pass.  Gate 164/5753.

THE THIRD CALLER was checked (rule 11, as the task asks): PExpr.pm's
negative-number splitter (`$prev_is_named_unary`, ~line 5913) now also answers
for a user unary sub, which is perl's reading -- `f -1` is f(-1) -- and is a
guard row.

PROBE RESIDUE, both PRE-EXISTING and filed separately: a BAREWORD operand to a
user prototyped sub is emitted as an unbound CL symbol for `(*)` (`fh FOO` ->
`(pl-fh FOO)`) and as a CALL to an undeclared sub for `($)` (`one BAR` ->
`(pl-one (pl-BAR))`), where perl gives the string; and `close G ? "a" : "b"`
is read as `close(G ? ...)` because the strictly-single bareword branch only
narrows before a comma or end.  Neither moved with this change (verified on
the worktree).
subject: A user NAMED-UNARY prototype's operand does not extend through `.`/`+`: `f "a" . "b"` is f("a")."b" for `($)`/`(;$)`/`(*)`/`(_)`; `(*)`'s `f + 1, "\n"` swallows the comma â the user operand site lacks the builtin site's _extend_high_prec (the two sites should be ONE)
